description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities. Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the Grant Obligations and Conditions, the obligatory dates for submission of the annual/additional reports are mentioned. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

comment.narrative:
The training courses / workshops will capacitate 63 staff and 9 Board members in understanding, prioritising and implementing performance improvement plans.
​
(1) 35 participants inspired and empowered through leadership training (Board and Senior Management);
(2) 20 participants trained in hydraulic engineering and energy calculations that will help optimize (and improve) water supply;
(3) 20 participants trained in understanding and applying basic asset management principles (gradual shift away from ‘firefighting’ to planned maintenance).
(4) 20 participants trained in NRW reduction (Data analysis / basic MS Excel, Water balance, Physical and Commercial losses, NRW Reduction Strategy/Plan and customer care).
(5) 20 participants trained in water treatment, optimisation of chemical dosing (to improve treated water quality and reduce chemical use) and basic plant maintenance.
(6) 12 participants trained in the development of 4 business cases for LgWSC using existing (billing system) and/or collected data.
17-05-2022: 2020-Q4 + 2021; number of participants x trainings; some trainings cover multiple days; minorities (or people with disabilities) are not specifically counted or considered (so no data)

title.narrative: B.O.4. Number of organisations developed and implemented a gender strategy

comment.narrative: 17-05-2022: Not requested. However, most Zambian water utilities have a gender / inlusion strategy of some sort. Gender equality is embedded in the Zambian constitution and all public sector organizations (water conpanies included) are stimulated to obtain equal gender representation. The underlying challenges are more cultural (traditional) in nature and the employers try to give the best example. Obtain gender equality will require (for thee water utilities) equal participation in (tertiary) education of men and women.
17-05-2022: not addressed yet, will be included in later training
